key_insight: Halide substitution in Ca3PX3 strongly tunes photovoltaic performance, with Ca3PI3 emerging as the most promising solar absorber due to its highest predicted efficiency.
engineering_relevance: This work highlights composition engineering as a practical route to optimize perovskite-like materials for next-generation solar cells and optoelectronic devices.
method: Electronic band structure analysis for direct bandgap assessment
Optical/spectroscopic screening limited maximum efficiency (SLME) evaluation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps across all compounds (2.0 to 3.788 eV) and identifies Ca3PI3 as the top performer with 29.6% SLME versus only 0.6% for Ca3PF3.
watch_item: The reported efficiencies are computational predictions, so experimental stability, defect tolerance, and device fabrication effects still need validation.
paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
